meta.title: If a Company Goes Bankrupt, Bondholders Get Paid Before Stockholders
meta.hook: If the company you invested in goes bankrupt, one type of investor gets paid before everyone else.
meta.description: A bond is a loan: a government or company borrows from investors and pays regular interest, called a coupon, returning the principal at maturity. Bondholders sit ahead of stockholders in a company's capital structure, meaning they're repaid first if the company fails. Safer borrowers can pay lower interest because investors demand less compensation for the risk. Educational content only, not financial advice.

scenes.narration: If the company you invested in goes bankrupt, one type of investor gets paid before everyone else.

visual.visual_intent: A close-up handshake over a desk with documents, warm light, symbolic of an agreement
visual.decision_reason: hook beat: reframing the common misconception

scenes.narration: A bond is an IOU. A government or company borrows from you and promises to pay it back.

visual.visual_intent: A government building facade, classic columns, daylight, wide shot

scenes.narration: In exchange, they pay you regular interest, called a coupon, until the bond matures.

visual.visual_intent: A calendar with recurring payment markers highlighted at intervals, clean graphic

scenes.narration: At maturity, you get your original loan amount back, assuming the borrower doesn't default.

visual.visual_intent: An envelope being opened revealing a document, symbolic of receiving payment, warm light
visual.decision_reason: defines maturity/principal return, notes default risk

scenes.narration: That's why bonds from the US government are considered safer than bonds from a struggling company.

visual.visual_intent: A US Treasury-style government building exterior, daylight, formal composition

scenes.narration: The safer the borrower, the lower the interest rate they can get away with paying you.

visual.visual_intent: A seesaw balancing two weighted sides, symbolic of risk versus reward, clean render

scenes.narration: And here's the investor you asked about. In a bankruptcy, bondholders are legally paid back before stockholders see a cent.

visual.visual_intent: A courthouse or legal building exterior, formal daylight, symbolic of legal priority
visual.decision_reason: capital-structure seniority: bondholders rank ahead of equity holders in liquidation, standard corporate-finance/bankruptcy-law principle

scenes.narration: Stocks make you an owner, last in line. Bonds make you a lender, first in line. Different risk, different reward.
